*They struck it with light garments, so you see it has no likeness except the startled ostrich.*

"They struck it," meaning the riders with their bodies.

And ʿAntarah said:

*So I pierced with the solid spear its garment; the noble one is not made unlawful by the spear.*

Meaning: himself.

In the narration of al-Kalbi: it means, "Do not be treacherous, for you would be a treacherous one with filthy garments."

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "When a man was treacherous, it was said: 'filthy garments, evil garments.'"

**[Chapter: Ibn al-Qayyim's Definition of Wara']**

The author of *al-Manazil* said:

"Wara' is a thorough guarding out of caution, and a scrupulous avoidance out of veneration."

He means: that one guards against the unlawful and the doubtful, and what he fears may harm him, to the utmost of his ability in guarding. For guarding (tawaqqi) and caution (hadhar) are close, except that guarding is an action of the limbs, and caution is an action of the heart. A servant may guard against something not out of caution and fear, but for other reasons, such as displaying dignity, pride, Sufi affectation, or some other objection. Like the guarding of those who do not believe in the Return, nor Paradise or Hellfire, against indecencies and baseness, out of protecting themselves from them, and desire of their souls to avoid them, and seeking praise, and the like.

His saying: "or a scrupulous avoidance out of veneration" means that the motive for wara' from the forbidden and the doubtful is either fear of the descent of the threat, or veneration of the Lord, Majestic is His majesty, and reverence for Him so that one does not approach what He has forbidden.

So wara' from disobedience is either fear or veneration. He suffices with mentioning veneration rather than mentioning love, which motivates leaving the disobedience of the beloved, because it does not exist except with veneration of Him. Otherwise, if the heart were empty of veneration of Him, love of Him would not necessitate abandoning opposition to Him, like a person's love for his child, his servant, or his female slave. When veneration accompanies it, it requires abandoning opposition.

He said: "And it is the last station of asceticism for the common people, and the first station of asceticism for the seeker (murid)."

He means that this guarding and scrupulousness, described by fear and veneration, is the end of the asceticism of the common people, and the beginning of the asceticism of the seeker. It is so because wara', as has preceded, is the beginning of asceticism and its pillar, and the asceticism of the seeker is above the asceticism of the common people. The end of the common people is the beginning of the seeker. So the end of the station of this is the beginning of the station of that. When the wara' of the common people ends, it becomes asceticism, and it is the first wara' of the seeker.

Yahya ibn Muʿadh said: "Wara' is standing at the limit of knowledge without interpretation." He also said: "Wara' is of two kinds: wara' of the outward and wara' of the inward. The wara' of the outward is that you do not move except for Allah, and the wara' of the inward is that you do not let anything other than Him enter your heart." He also said: "Whoever does not look into the subtle aspects of wara' will not reach the grand gifts."

It was said: "Wara' is departing from desires and abandoning misdeeds."

It was said: "Whoever's wara' or insight is subtle in this world, his worth will be great on the Day of Resurrection."

Yunus ibn ʿUbayd said: "Wara' is departing from every doubt, and taking account of oneself in every blink of an eye."

Sufyan al-Thawri said: "I have never seen anything easier than wara': whatever stirs in your soul, leave it."

Sahl said: "The lawful is that in which Allah is not disobeyed, and the pure of it is that in which Allah is not forgotten." Al-Hasan asked a boy: "What is the foundation of religion?" He said: "Wara'." He said: "What is its blight?" He said: "Greed." Al-Hasan was amazed at him.

Al-Hasan said: "An atom's weight of wara' is better than a thousand weights of fasting and prayer."

Abu Hurayrah said: "The companions of Allah tomorrow are the people of wara' and asceticism."

One of the early generation said: "The servant does not reach the reality of taqwa until he leaves what has no harm in it, out of fear of what has harm in it."

One of the Companions said: "We used to leave seventy doors of the lawful, for fear of falling into one door of the unlawful."

**[Chapter: Ibn al-Qayyim's Definition of Wara']**

The author of *al-Manazil* said:

"Wara' is a thorough guarding out of caution, and a scrupulous avoidance out of veneration."

He means: that one guards against the unlawful and the doubtful, and what he fears may harm him, to the utmost of his ability in guarding. For guarding (tawaqqi) and caution (hadhar) are close, except that guarding is an action of the limbs, and caution is an action of the heart. A servant may guard against something not out of caution and fear, but for other reasons, such as displaying dignity, pride, Sufi affectation, or some other objection. Like the guarding of those who do not believe in the Return, nor Paradise or Hellfire, against indecencies and baseness, out of protecting themselves from them, and desire of their souls to avoid them, and seeking praise, and the like.

His saying: "or a scrupulous avoidance out of veneration" means that the motive for wara' from the forbidden and the doubtful is either fear of the descent of the threat, or veneration of the Lord, Majestic is His majesty, and reverence for Him so that one does not approach what He has forbidden.

So wara' from disobedience is either fear or veneration. He suffices with mentioning veneration rather than mentioning love, which motivates leaving the disobedience of the beloved, because it does not exist except with veneration of Him. Otherwise, if the heart were empty of veneration of Him, love of Him would not necessitate abandoning opposition to Him, like a person's love for his child, his servant, or his female slave. When veneration accompanies it, it requires abandoning opposition.

He said: "And it is the last station of asceticism for the common people, and the first station of asceticism for the seeker (murid)."

He means that this guarding and scrupulousness, described by fear and veneration, is the end of the asceticism of the common people, and the beginning of the asceticism of the seeker. It is so because wara', as has preceded, is the beginning of asceticism and its pillar, and the asceticism of the seeker is above the asceticism of the common people. The end of the common people is the beginning of the seeker. So the end of the station of this is the beginning of the station of that. When the wara' of the common people ends, it becomes asceticism, and it is the first wara' of the seeker.
Scholars of tafsir among the early generations and those after them said: "Do not give a gift seeking more in return", which means giving a gift so that you are given back more than what you gave.

Allah, glory be to Him, informed us of the wisdom for which the number of angels appointed over the Fire was made nineteen, and He mentioned five wisdoms:

The first is the trial of the disbelievers, so that this becomes an increase in their disbelief and misguidance.

The second is the strengthening of the certainty of the People of the Book. Their certainty is strengthened because the report agrees with what they have from their prophets, without having received it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about them, so the proof is established against those who are obstinate among them.

The third is that whoever Allah wills to guide submits to faith.

The fourth is the increase in faith of those who believe, through their complete acceptance of this and their affirmation of it.

The fifth is the removal of doubt from the People of the Book, because they are certain of it, and from the believers, because of their complete acceptance of it.

These are four wisdoms: the trial of the disbelievers, the certainty of the People of the Book, the increase in the faith of the believers, and the removal of doubt from the believers and the People of the Book.

The fifth is the bewilderment of the disbeliever and of the one in whose heart is a disease, and the blindness of his heart to what is meant by this, so he says: ﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26].

This is the state of hearts when the truth sent down to them arrives. There is a heart that is tried by it into disbelief and denial. There is a heart that increases in faith and affirmation through it. There is a heart that is certain of it, so the proof is established upon it. And there is a heart for which it brings bewilderment and blindness, so it does not know what is meant by it.

As for certainty and the absence of doubt in this context: if the two refer to one thing, then mentioning the absence of doubt confirms and emphasizes the certainty and negates anything contrary to it in some respect. If they refer to two things, such that certainty refers to the report mentioned about the number of the angels, and the absence of doubt refers to the whole of what the Messenger reported, because this report, which is known only through the messengers, indicates its truth, then whoever has recognized the soundness of this report after the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ) will not doubt, and the benefit of mentioning it becomes clear.

The purpose is: mentioning the disease of the heart and its reality.

Because in its departure and the advance of the day lies among the clearest manifest proofs of the origin and the return. It is a daily origin and return witnessed by sight: while living beings are in the stillness of the night, their movements have ceased, their voices are silent, and their eyes are asleep, and they become like brothers of the dead; then the day comes with its caller, and it makes the creatures hear its herald. Movements spread among them and voices rise, until it is as if they rose alive from the graves, one of them saying, "Praise be to God, who gave us life after He had made us die, and to Him is the resurrection." Whoever contemplates the state of the night when it draws on and departs, and the morning when it breathes and brightens, who routs the armies of darkness by itself, lights the horizon of the world with its ember, scatters the battalions of the stars with its hosts, and makes the regions of the earth laugh with its harbingers and glad tidings — how marvelous these are, two signs bearing witness to the oneness of their Originator, the perfection of His lordship, the greatness of His power and wisdom. Blessed is He who made the rising and setting of the sun the establishment of the sovereignty of night and day.

Were it not for its rising, the affairs of the whole world would be void. How would people strive in their livelihoods and manage their affairs while the world was dark to them?

And how would life be pleasant with the loss of the delight and spirit of light?

What fruits, plants, and animals would exist? And how would the interests of the bodies of animals and plants be accomplished? And were it not for its setting, people would have no rest or repose, though it is known that they need rest for the comfort of their bodies and the stilling of their senses.

Were it not for this night settling upon them with its darkness, they would not rest, nor be comforted, nor be still. Rather, the Most Wise of the wise made it a repose and a garment, just as He made the day a light and a means of livelihood. Were it not for the night and its coolness, the bodies of plants and animals would be burned by the constant shining of the sun upon them, and whatever plants and animals were upon them would be scorched. So the wisdom of the Most Wise of the wise required that He made it a lamp which rises upon the world at the time they need it and sets at the time they are free of it. Its rising is for their benefit and its setting is for their benefit. Light and darkness, though opposed, have become cooperating and mutually supportive for the benefit and sustenance of this world. Had God, glorified is He, made the day perpetual until the Day of Resurrection and the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, the interests of the world would have perished, and there would have been urgent need to change that and remove it by its opposite.

Consider His wisdom, glorified is He, in the rising and falling of the sun to establish these four seasons of the year and what that contains of the interests of creation. In winter, heat recedes into trees and plants, so fruit substances form from it; the air condenses, so clouds form from it and gather into rain, by which the earth lives and the bodies of animals and plants grow, and by which faculties and natural powers and the movements of natures are accomplished. In summer, the air is hot, so fruits ripen, grains harden, and the surface of the earth is dried so that work is made possible. In autumn, the air clears, the heat cools, the night lengthens, and the earth and trees rest for bearing, and plants recover a second time, like the rest of a pregnant woman between two pregnancies. In these seasons there is a visible origin and return, and a witness to the unseen origin and return.

The point is that by the movement of these two luminaries the interests of the world are accomplished, and through this time becomes manifest, for time is the measure of motion. The solar year is the measure of the sun's course from the point of Aries back to its like, and the lunar year is measured by the course of the moon, which is closer to precision, and people share knowledge of it. The Most Wise of the wise decreed their transitions through their stations, for in that is perfect wisdom and subtle arrangement. Had the sun risen and set in one place without exceeding it, its light and rays would not have reached many regions, and its benefit would have been lost there. So God, glorified is He, made its rising circulate around the earth, so that its benefit and influence reach all regions, and there remains no place on which it could rise without taking its share of its benefit. This perfect arrangement required that the length of night and day be set at twenty-four hours, each taking from the other, and the extent of each when it is lengthened being fifteen hours. Had the length of the day exceeded this, say to fifty hours or more, the order of the world would have been disrupted and most animals and plants would have been corrupted; and had its length been reduced below this, the order would likewise have been disrupted and interests would have been suspended. Had they been equal permanently, the seasons of the year would not have varied, and with their variation the interests of servants and animals are tied. So in this measured and perfect determination and arrangement there are signs, interests, and benefits which testify that this is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. For this reason He mentions this determination and attributes it to His might and knowledge, as He said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs to its resting place; that is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ And He said: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly. Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and inspired in every heaven its command, and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ And He said: ﴿Cleaver of the dawn, and He made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

These are three places in which He mentions that the determination of the movements of the sun and the moon and the celestial bodies and what results from them was by the requirement of His might and knowledge, and that He determined it by these two attributes. In this is a refutation of the enemies of God, the atheists, who deny His power, His choice, and His knowledge of the unseen.

For the servant, in every one of his limbs, God has a command, and God has a prohibition concerning it, and God has a blessing in it, and God has a benefit and pleasure in it.

If he stands before God in that limb by His command, and avoids His prohibition concerning it, he has given thanks for His blessing upon it, and has striven to perfect his benefit and pleasure from it.

If he neglects God's command and prohibition concerning it, God will deprive him of benefit from that limb, and make it one of the greatest causes of his pain and harm.

And for Him, in every moment of his time, there is a servitude which advances him and brings him near to Him. If he occupies his time with the servitude of that moment, he advances toward his Lord; if he occupies it with the desires of his spirit and idleness, he lags behind. He, glorified is He, has mentioned this in three verses of His Book. The first is His saying: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: They are timings for the people and for the Pilgrimage.﴾ The second is His saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. God did not create that except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.﴾ The third is His saying: ﴿We made the night and the day two signs, and We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day illuminating, that you might seek bounty from your Lord and that you might know the number of years and the reckoning; and everything We have detailed with full detail.﴾ So were it not for what God, glorified is He, causes in the signs of the night of increase and decrease of its light, the appointed time of the Pilgrimage, the fast, the waiting period, the period of nursing, the period of pregnancy, the term of hire, and the terms of pregnant women would not be known.

If it is said: Could this have been achieved by the movement of the sun and the days that are preserved by the sunrise and sunset, as the People of the Two Books know the appointed times of their fasts and festivals by solar reckoning?

It is said: Although this is possible, it is difficult to regulate, and only individuals among people can master it. There is no doubt that knowing the beginnings, middles, and ends of the months by the moon is a matter in which people share; it is easier than knowing that by solar reckoning, and less subject to disturbance and disagreement, and it requires no laborious calculation, nor does the one who does not know it have to follow him who knows it. So the consummate wisdom in determining the years and months by the course of the moon is more evident, more beneficial, more suitable, and less disputed than determining them by the course of the sun. The Lord, majestic is His majesty, arranged the crescents with this wondrous arrangement for the benefit of His creation in the interests of their religion and their worldly life, together with what is connected to it of inference of the oneness of the Lord and the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge, and arrangement. So the testimony of truth lies in the changing of the celestial bodies, and the proofs of their createdness and origination stand upon them. They are signs speaking through the tongue of state, refuting the materialists, the zindiq philosophers, and the atheists who claim that they are eternal and everlasting, not subject to change, and that their non-existence is impossible.

When the discerning observer contemplates the moon, for instance, its need of a locus in which to subsist, its perpetual motion that never slackens, a motion of one subjected and arranged, its descent at times, its ascent at times, its setting at times, its appearance at times, the gradual departure of its light and its return in the same way, and the source of its light being one whole, until it returns as a dark piece through eclipse, he knows with certainty that it is created, lordly, subjected, under the command of a Creator, Irresistible, who subjects it as He wills. He knows that the Lord, glorified is He, did not create this in vain, that this motion in it must inevitably end in cessation and stillness, that this light must inevitably end in its opposite, and that this dominion must inevitably end in dismissal. He will gather the two together, the Gatherer of scattered things, after they were not gathered, and will take them wherever He wills. He will show the polytheists who worship them the state of their gods which they worshipped besides Him, just as He shows the worshippers of the stars the scattering of the stars, the worshippers of heaven the splitting of heaven, the worshippers of the sun its folding up, and the worshippers of idols their humiliation, and their being cast into the Fire as the most worthless, abject, and lowly thing. Just as I show the worshippers of the calf in this world its state, that it is ground, and its worshippers crush and annihilate it, and the wind scatters and disperses it into the sea. And just as I show the idols in this world, their images broken and shattered, cast in filthy places, and the hammers of the monotheists have smashed those faces, broken those heads, and cut off those hands and feet which could not be approached except by kissing and touching. This is the unchanging custom of God and His unalterable practice: He shows the worshipper of other than Him the state of his worshipped object in this world and the Hereafter, even if the object does not approve of being worshipped, and He shows him its disavowal of him and its hostility toward him at the moment he most needs it: ﴿that whoever perished might perish by clear proof, and whoever lives might live by clear proof.﴾

﴿and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.﴾

Reflect upon the lines of existence, for they are from the Supreme King, messages to you.
And He has inscribed in them, if you reflect upon their script: "Surely everything other than God is vain."

Had the Exalted willed, He would have kept the moon in one unchanging state and made change in the sun; had He willed, He would have changed both together; and had He willed, He would have kept both in one state. But He shows His servants His signs in the various kinds of their transformations, so that they know Him as God, there is no god but He, the King, the Manifest Truth, the Doer of what He wills: ﴿Surely, to Him belong creation and command; blessed is God, Lord of the worlds.﴾ As for the moon's influence on moistening the bodies of animals and plants, on the waters, on the ebb and flow of the sea, on the crises of diseases and their transfer from one state to another, and other benefits, that is manifest.

(Section)

As for His swearing, glorified is He, by: ﴿and the night when it departs﴾

Because in its departure and the advance of the day lies among the clearest manifest proofs of the origin and the return. It is a daily origin and return witnessed by sight: while living beings are in the stillness of the night, their movements have ceased, their voices are silent, and their eyes are asleep, and they become like brothers of the dead; then the day comes with its caller, and it makes the creatures hear its herald. Movements spread among them and voices rise, until it is as if they rose alive from the graves, one of them saying, "Praise be to God, who gave us life after He had made us die, and to Him is the resurrection." So it is a new return which He began and repeats, the One who originates and restores. Whoever takes away the night and brings the day, other than the One, the Subduer?

Whoever contemplates the state of the night when it draws on and departs, and the morning when it breathes and brightens, who routs the armies of darkness by itself, lights the horizon of the world with its ember, scatters the battalions of the stars with its hosts, and makes the regions of the earth laugh with its harbingers and glad tidings — how marvelous these are, two signs bearing witness to the oneness of their Originator, the perfection of His lordship, the greatness of His power and wisdom. Blessed is He who made the rising and setting of the sun the establishment of the sovereignty of night and day.

Were it not for its rising, the affairs of the whole world would be void. How would people strive in their livelihoods and manage their affairs while the world was dark to them?

And how would life be pleasant with the loss of the delight and spirit of light?

What fruits, plants, and animals would exist? And how would the interests of the bodies of animals and plants be accomplished? And were it not for its setting, people would have no rest or repose, though it is known that they need rest for the comfort of their bodies and the stilling of their senses.

Were it not for this night settling upon them with its darkness, they would not rest, nor be comforted, nor be still. Rather, the Most Wise of the wise made it a repose and a garment, just as He made the day a light and a means of livelihood. Were it not for the night and its coolness, the bodies of plants and animals would be burned by the constant shining of the sun upon them, and whatever plants and animals were upon them would be scorched. So the wisdom of the Most Wise of the wise required that He made it a lamp which rises upon the world at the time they need it and sets at the time they are free of it. Its rising is for their benefit and its setting is for their benefit. Light and darkness, though opposed, have become cooperating and mutually supportive for the benefit and sustenance of this world. Had God, glorified is He, made the day perpetual until the Day of Resurrection and the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, the interests of the world would have perished, and there would have been urgent need to change that and remove it by its opposite.

Consider His wisdom, glorified is He, in the rising and falling of the sun to establish these four seasons of the year and what that contains of the interests of creation. In winter, heat recedes into trees and plants, so fruit substances form from it; the air condenses, so clouds form from it and gather into rain, by which the earth lives and the bodies of animals and plants grow, and by which faculties and natural powers and the movements of natures are accomplished. In summer, the air is hot, so fruits ripen, grains harden, and the surface of the earth is dried so that work is made possible. In autumn, the air clears, the heat cools, the night lengthens, and the earth and trees rest for bearing, and plants recover a second time, like the rest of a pregnant woman between two pregnancies. In these seasons there is a visible origin and return, and a witness to the unseen origin and return.

The point is that by the movement of these two luminaries the interests of the world are accomplished, and through this time becomes manifest, for time is the measure of motion. The solar year is the measure of the sun's course from the point of Aries back to its like, and the lunar year is measured by the course of the moon, which is closer to precision, and people share knowledge of it. The Most Wise of the wise decreed their transitions through their stations, for in that is perfect wisdom and subtle arrangement. Had the sun risen and set in one place without exceeding it, its light and rays would not have reached many regions, and its benefit would have been lost there. So God, glorified is He, made its rising circulate around the earth, so that its benefit and influence reach all regions, and there remains no place on which it could rise without taking its share of its benefit. This perfect arrangement required that the length of night and day be set at twenty-four hours, each taking from the other, and the extent of each when it is lengthened being fifteen hours. Had the length of the day exceeded this, say to fifty hours or more, the order of the world would have been disrupted and most animals and plants would have been corrupted; and had its length been reduced below this, the order would likewise have been disrupted and interests would have been suspended. Had they been equal permanently, the seasons of the year would not have varied, and with their variation the interests of servants and animals are tied. So in this measured and perfect determination and arrangement there are signs, interests, and benefits which testify that this is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. For this reason He mentions this determination and attributes it to His might and knowledge, as He said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs to its resting place; that is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ And He said: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly. Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and inspired in every heaven its command, and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ And He said: ﴿Cleaver of the dawn, and He made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the determination of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

These are three places in which He mentions that the determination of the movements of the sun and the moon and the celestial bodies and what results from them was by the requirement of His might and knowledge, and that He determined it by these two attributes. In this is a refutation of the enemies of God, the atheists, who deny His power, His choice, and His knowledge of the unseen.

But the wrongdoers refused except disbelief: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods which create nothing, and are themselves created, and possess no power to harm or benefit themselves, and possess no power over death or life or resurrection.﴾ ﴿for whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind.﴾ (37)

(Exhortation)

For the servant, in every one of his limbs, God has a command, and God has a prohibition concerning it, and God has a blessing in it, and God has a benefit and pleasure in it.

If he stands before God in that limb by His command, and avoids His prohibition concerning it, he has given thanks for His blessing upon it, and has striven to perfect his benefit and pleasure from it.

If he neglects God's command and prohibition concerning it, God will deprive him of benefit from that limb, and make it one of the greatest causes of his pain and harm.

And for Him, in every moment of his time, there is a servitude which advances him and brings him near to Him. If he occupies his time with the servitude of that moment, he advances toward his Lord; if he occupies it with the desires of his spirit and idleness, he lags behind. The servant never ceases to be advancing or lagging, and there is absolutely no standing still on the path. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿for whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind.﴾

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 74, verses 38–39:**

When Allah had established the proof and made the argument clear, every soul was held in pledge for what it earned and was seized for its sin. He excepted from them those who had gone before in His guidance and followed His good pleasure. These are the People of the Right (ashab al-yamin), who believed in Allah, affirmed the Messengers, and took a path other than the path of the criminals, who were not among those who prayed and did not feed the needy. They were among those who plunged into falsehood with the plungers, who denied the Day of Judgement. So these are four qualities that removed them from the company of the successful and placed them among the doomed. The first is abandoning the prayer, which is the pillar of sincere devotion to the One worshipped. The second is abandoning the feeding of the needy, which is one of the levels of goodness toward creatures. Without sincerity toward the Creator there is no sincerity toward creation, and without goodness toward the created there is no goodness toward creatures, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who make a show of their deeds and withhold small kindnesses.﴾ (Al-Ma'un: 6–7)

He also said: ﴿And they do not come to prayer except lazily, and they do not spend except unwillingly.﴾ (At-Tawbah: 54)

This is the opposite of what He described of the People of the Right when He said: ﴿Those who establish prayer and spend of what We have provided for them.﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 3)

And He said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend of what We have provided for them.﴾ (As-Sajdah: 16)

Allah, glory be to Him, joined these two foundations in many places in His Book. At times He commanded them, at times He praised those who perform them, and at times He threatened with woe and punishment those who abandon them. The means of salvation revolve around these two, and there is no success for one who neglects them.

**(Benefit)**

**The meaning of "Every boy is held in pledge by his 'aqiqah"**

He (ﷺ) said: "Every boy is held in pledge by his 'aqiqah ('aqiqah: the sacrifice made for a newborn), which is slaughtered for him on the seventh day, his head is shaved, and he is named."

Imam Ahmad said: Its meaning is that he is withheld from intercession on behalf of his parents. Al-rahn (pledge) in the language means confinement. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned.﴾ (Al-Muddaththir: 38)

The apparent meaning of the hadith is that he is held in pledge in himself, prevented and confined from a good intended for him. This does not necessarily mean that he will be punished for it in the Hereafter. He may be confined, by his parents' neglect of the 'aqiqah, from what he would have attained had his parents performed it on his behalf. Good may also be lost to a child through the negligence of his parents, even if it is not from his own earning. Just as, at intercourse, if his father mentions the name of Allah, Satan does not harm the child, and if he omits the mention of the name, the child does not receive this protection.

Furthermore, this indicates that the 'aqiqah is obligatory and unavoidable, and so the child's being bound to it and not being separated from it is likened to a pledge. Those who hold it to be obligatory, such as al-Layth ibn Sa'd, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ahl al-Zahir (the Zahiri school, which takes the apparent meaning of texts), may use this as evidence. And Allah knows best.

**(Benefits and Admonitions)**

**(Section: From the sayings of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him)**

A man said in his presence: "I do not wish to be among the People of the Right; I wish to be among those brought near."

Abdullah said: "But here is a man who loved (to be among them) and wished that he would die without being raised."

He meant himself.

One day he went out, and people followed him. He said to them: "Do you have a need?" They said: "No, but we wanted to walk with you."

He said: "Go back, for it is humiliation for the follower and a trial for the one followed."

He also said: "If you knew of me what I know of myself, you would throw dust on my head."

He also said: "How hateful are the two disliked things, death and poverty! By Allah, it is nothing but wealth and poverty, and I do not care which of the two I am afflicted with. I hope for Allah's reward in each of them: if it is wealth, there is in it kindness (to others); if it is poverty, there is in it patience."

He also said: "You are in the passing of the night and the day, in limited lifespans and recorded deeds, and death comes suddenly. So whoever plants good will soon reap what he desires. Whoever plants evil will soon reap regret. Every planter gets what he has planted. The slow one does not gain by his share, and the eager one does not reach what has not been decreed for him. Whoever is given good, Allah has given it to him, and whoever is protected from evil, Allah has protected him."

"The God-fearing are masters, the jurists are leaders, and sitting with them is an increase."

"There are only two things: guidance and speech. The best speech is the speech of Allah, the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is a bid'ah (innovation in religion)."

"Let the long time not draw out upon you, nor hope distract you, for everything that is coming is near. The distant time is what has not yet come. The wretched one is he who was wretched in his mother's womb, and the happy one is he who takes admonition from others."

"Beware, fighting a Muslim is disbelief, cursing him is sin, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days. He should greet him when he meets him, answer him when he calls him, and visit him when he is ill."

"Beware, the worst of vessels is the vessel of lies. Beware, lying is not fit in any part, neither in seriousness nor in jest, nor for a man to promise his child something and then not fulfil it."

"Beware, lying leads to wickedness, wickedness leads to the Fire, truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. The truthful man is called truthful and righteous, and the liar is called a liar and a wicked one."

Muhammad (ﷺ) told us that a man would tell the truth until he is written before Allah as truthful, and would lie until he is written before Allah as a liar.

"The truest speech is the Book of Allah, the firmest handhold is the word of piety, the best religion is the religion of Abraham, the best way is the way of Muhammad (ﷺ), the best guidance is the guidance of the Prophets, the most noble speech is the remembrance of Allah, the best accounts are the Qur'an, the best of matters are their outcomes, and the worst of matters are their innovations."

"What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting."

"A soul that you save is better than a rule you cannot count. The worst excuse is when death arrives. The worst regret is the regret of the Day of Resurrection. The worst misguidance is misguidance after desire. The best wealth is the wealth of the soul. The best provision is piety. The best thing cast into the heart is certainty. Doubt is from disbelief. The worst blindness is blindness of the heart. Wine is the sum of sin. Women are the snares of Satan. Youth is a branch of madness. Wailing is an act of the days of ignorance."

"Among the people is one who does not come to the Friday prayer except late, and does not remember Allah except rarely."

"The greatest of sins is lying. Whoever forgives, Allah will forgive him. Whoever restrains anger, Allah will reward him. Whoever forgives, Allah will forgive him. Whoever is patient in calamity, Allah will recompense him. The worst earnings are the earnings of usury. The worst food is the property of an orphan. It is enough for one of you what his soul is content with. He will end up in four cubits (of earth), and the matter goes to its end. The worth of an action is in its endings. The most noble death is death as a martyr."

"Whoever is arrogant, Allah will abase him, and whoever disobeys Allah, obeys Satan."

"The bearer of the Qur'an should be recognised by his night when people are asleep, by his day when people are fasting, by his sorrow when people are rejoicing, by his weeping when people are laughing, by his silence when people are indulging, and by his humility when people are strutting."

"The bearer of the Qur'an should be weeping, sorrowful, wise, forbearing, and tranquil. He should not be harsh, nor heedless, nor clamorous, nor loud, nor quarrelsome."

"Whoever exalts himself out of pride, Allah will humble him, and whoever humbles himself out of reverence, Allah will raise him. The angel has an inspiration (lamma), and Satan has an inspiration. The angel's inspiration is a promise of good and affirmation of the truth. When you experience that, praise Allah. Satan's inspiration is a promise of evil and denial of the truth. When you experience that, seek refuge in Allah."

"People have spoken well. Whoever's speech agrees with his deeds, that is the one who has attained his share. Whoever's speech contradicts his deeds, he is only reproaching himself."

"Let me not find any of you a corpse of the night, a dweller of the day (i.e., idle, neglectful). I dislike a man whom I see idle, not engaged in any work of this world or of the next. Whoever is not commanded by his prayer to do good and not restrained from evil, has only increased his distance from Allah."

"Of certainty is that you do not please people by angering Allah, nor praise anyone for the provision of Allah, nor blame anyone for what Allah has not given you. The provision of Allah is not driven by the greed of the greedy, nor turned away by the dislike of the disliker. Allah, by His justice, forbearance, and fairness, has placed comfort and joy in certainty and contentment, and placed grief and anguish in doubt and discontent."

"As long as you are in prayer, you are knocking at the door of the King, and whoever knocks at the door of the King, it is opened to him."

"I think a man forgets the knowledge he used to teach because of the sin he commits."

"Be springs of knowledge, lamps of guidance, stayers at home, lamps of the night, fresh of heart, and worn of garment. You are known in the heavens and unknown among the people of the earth."

"Hearts have appetite and aversion, so seize them at their appetite and their advance, and leave them at their dispersal and their retreat."

"Knowledge is not in the abundance of narration, but knowledge is fear (of Allah). You see the disbeliever as the healthiest of people in body and the sickest in heart, and you meet the believer as the healthiest of people in heart and the sickest in body. By Allah, if your hearts were sick and your bodies healthy, you would be more insignificant to Allah than dung beetles."

"A servant will not attain the reality of faith until he reaches its summit, and he will not reach its summit until poverty is more beloved to him than wealth, humility more beloved to him than nobility, and until his praiser and his blamer are equal in his eyes."

"A man may leave his house with his religion in his possession and return with nothing of it remaining."

"A man comes to someone who owns neither harm nor benefit for himself or for others, and swears to him by Allah that you have become rich and unlucky (or: you have become stale), so he returns with nothing of his need satisfied, and Allah is displeased with him."

"If I were to mock a dog, I would fear being transformed into a dog."

"Sin is what pulls at the hearts. Whatever is a glance, Satan has a desire in it."

"With every joy is a sorrow, and no house is filled with delight except that it is filled with lessons. Not one of you is other than a guest, and his property is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned to its owners."

"At the end of time there will be people whose best deeds are blaming one another, who are called al-Antan (the foul-smelling ones)."

"If a man wishes to be treated justly by himself, let him treat people as he wishes to be treated."

"Truth is heavy but wholesome, and falsehood is light but harmful."

"Many a desire brings long sorrow."

"Nothing on the face of the earth needs a long imprisonment more than the tongue."

"When fornication and usury appear in a town, it has been permitted its destruction."

"Whoever among you can make his treasure in heaven, where moths do not eat it and thieves do not reach it, let him do so, for the heart of a man is with his treasure."

"Let none of you make his religion dependent on a man: if he believes, you believe, and if he disbelieves, you disbelieve. If you must follow, then follow the dead, for the living is not safe from trial."

"Do not be an imma'a (a person without a mind of his own, a mere follower)."

They said: "What is the imma'a?"

He said: "He says, 'I am with the people: if they are guided, I am guided, and if they go astray, I go astray.' Rather, let each of you resolve that if the people disbelieve, he will not disbelieve."

A man said to him: "Teach me comprehensive and beneficial words."

He said: "Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him. Stay with the Qur'an wherever it goes. Whoever brings you the truth, accept it from him even if he is distant and hateful, and whoever brings you falsehood, reject it even if he is beloved and close."

A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: "Render your trust." He will say: "O Lord, from where, when the world has gone?" Then it will take the form of its appearance on the day he took it, in the depth of Hell. He will slip and take it, place it upon his shoulder, and climb with it until, when he thinks he is out with it, it will fall, and he will fall after it forever and ever.

"Seek your heart in three places: at the hearing of the Qur'an, in gatherings of remembrance, and in times of solitude. If you do not find it in these places, ask Allah to bestow a heart upon you, for you have no heart."

**(Benefits and Admonitions)**

**(Section: From the sayings of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him)**

A man said in his presence: "I do not wish to be among the People of the Right; I wish to be among those brought near."

Abdullah said: "But here is a man who loved (to be among them) and wished that he would die without being raised."

He meant himself.

One day he went out, and people followed him. He said to them: "Do you have a need?" They said: "No, but we wanted to walk with you."

He said: "Go back, for it is humiliation for the follower and a trial for the one followed."

He also said: "If you knew of me what I know of myself, you would throw dust on my head."

He also said: "How hateful are the two disliked things, death and poverty! By Allah, it is nothing but wealth and poverty, and I do not care which of the two I am afflicted with. I hope for Allah's reward in each of them: if it is wealth, there is in it kindness (to others); if it is poverty, there is in it patience."

He also said: "You are in the passing of the night and the day, in limited lifespans and recorded deeds, and death comes suddenly. So whoever plants good will soon reap what he desires. Whoever plants evil will soon reap regret. Every planter gets what he has planted. The slow one does not gain by his share, and the eager one does not reach what has not been decreed for him. Whoever is given good, Allah has given it to him, and whoever is protected from evil, Allah has protected him."

"The God-fearing are masters, the jurists are leaders, and sitting with them is an increase."

"There are only two things: guidance and speech. The best speech is the speech of Allah, the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is a bid'ah (innovation in religion)."

"Let the long time not draw out upon you, nor hope distract you, for everything that is coming is near. The distant time is what has not yet come. The wretched one is he who was wretched in his mother's womb, and the happy one is he who takes admonition from others."

"Beware, fighting a Muslim is disbelief, cursing him is sin, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days. He should greet him when he meets him, answer him when he calls him, and visit him when he is ill."

"Beware, the worst of vessels is the vessel of lies. Beware, lying is not fit in any part, neither in seriousness nor in jest, nor for a man to promise his child something and then not fulfil it."

"Beware, lying leads to wickedness, wickedness leads to the Fire, truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. The truthful man is called truthful and righteous, and the liar is called a liar and a wicked one."

Muhammad (ﷺ) told us that a man would tell the truth until he is written before Allah as truthful, and would lie until he is written before Allah as a liar.

"The truest speech is the Book of Allah, the firmest handhold is the word of piety, the best religion is the religion of Abraham, the best way is the way of Muhammad (ﷺ), the best guidance is the guidance of the Prophets, the most noble speech is the remembrance of Allah, the best accounts are the Qur'an, the best of matters are their outcomes, and the worst of matters are their innovations."

"What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting."

"A soul that you save is better than a rule you cannot count. The worst excuse is when death arrives. The worst regret is the regret of the Day of Resurrection. The worst misguidance is misguidance after desire. The best wealth is the wealth of the soul. The best provision is piety. The best thing cast into the heart is certainty. Doubt is from disbelief. The worst blindness is blindness of the heart. Wine is the sum of sin. Women are the snares of Satan. Youth is a branch of madness. Wailing is an act of the days of ignorance."

"Among the people is one who does not come to the Friday prayer except late, and does not remember Allah except rarely."

"The greatest of sins is lying. Whoever forgives, Allah will forgive him. Whoever restrains anger, Allah will reward him. Whoever forgives, Allah will forgive him. Whoever is patient in calamity, Allah will recompense him. The worst earnings are the earnings of usury. The worst food is the property of an orphan. It is enough for one of you what his soul is content with. He will end up in four cubits (of earth), and the matter goes to its end. The worth of an action is in its endings. The most noble death is death as a martyr."

"Whoever is arrogant, Allah will abase him, and whoever disobeys Allah, obeys Satan."

"The bearer of the Qur'an should be recognised by his night when people are asleep, by his day when people are fasting, by his sorrow when people are rejoicing, by his weeping when people are laughing, by his silence when people are indulging, and by his humility when people are strutting."

"The bearer of the Qur'an should be weeping, sorrowful, wise, forbearing, and tranquil. He should not be harsh, nor heedless, nor clamorous, nor loud, nor quarrelsome."

"Whoever exalts himself out of pride, Allah will humble him, and whoever humbles himself out of reverence, Allah will raise him. The angel has an inspiration (lamma), and Satan has an inspiration. The angel's inspiration is a promise of good and affirmation of the truth. When you experience that, praise Allah. Satan's inspiration is a promise of evil and denial of the truth. When you experience that, seek refuge in Allah."

"People have spoken well. Whoever's speech agrees with his deeds, that is the one who has attained his share. Whoever's speech contradicts his deeds, he is only reproaching himself."

"Let me not find any of you a corpse of the night, a dweller of the day (i.e., idle, neglectful). I dislike a man whom I see idle, not engaged in any work of this world or of the next. Whoever is not commanded by his prayer to do good and not restrained from evil, has only increased his distance from Allah."

"Of certainty is that you do not please people by angering Allah, nor praise anyone for the provision of Allah, nor blame anyone for what Allah has not given you. The provision of Allah is not driven by the greed of the greedy, nor turned away by the dislike of the disliker. Allah, by His justice, forbearance, and fairness, has placed comfort and joy in certainty and contentment, and placed grief and anguish in doubt and discontent."

"As long as you are in prayer, you are knocking at the door of the King, and whoever knocks at the door of the King, it is opened to him."

"I think a man forgets the knowledge he used to teach because of the sin he commits."

"Be springs of knowledge, lamps of guidance, stayers at home, lamps of the night, fresh of heart, and worn of garment. You are known in the heavens and unknown among the people of the earth."

"Hearts have appetite and aversion, so seize them at their appetite and their advance, and leave them at their dispersal and their retreat."

"Knowledge is not in the abundance of narration, but knowledge is fear (of Allah). You see the disbeliever as the healthiest of people in body and the sickest in heart, and you meet the believer as the healthiest of people in heart and the sickest in body. By Allah, if your hearts were sick and your bodies healthy, you would be more insignificant to Allah than dung beetles."

"A servant will not attain the reality of faith until he reaches its summit, and he will not reach its summit until poverty is more beloved to him than wealth, humility more beloved to him than nobility, and until his praiser and his blamer are equal in his eyes."

"A man may leave his house with his religion in his possession and return with nothing of it remaining."

"A man comes to someone who owns neither harm nor benefit for himself or for others, and swears to him by Allah that you have become rich and unlucky (or: you have become stale), so he returns with nothing of his need satisfied, and Allah is displeased with him."

"If I were to mock a dog, I would fear being transformed into a dog."

"Sin is what pulls at the hearts. Whatever is a glance, Satan has a desire in it."

"With every joy is a sorrow, and no house is filled with delight except that it is filled with lessons. Not one of you is other than a guest, and his property is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned to its owners."

"At the end of time there will be people whose best deeds are blaming one another, who are called al-Antan (the foul-smelling ones)."

"If a man wishes to be treated justly by himself, let him treat people as he wishes to be treated."

"Truth is heavy but wholesome, and falsehood is light but harmful."

"Many a desire brings long sorrow."

"Nothing on the face of the earth needs a long imprisonment more than the tongue."

"When fornication and usury appear in a town, it has been permitted its destruction."

"Whoever among you can make his treasure in heaven, where moths do not eat it and thieves do not reach it, let him do so, for the heart of a man is with his treasure."

"Let none of you make his religion dependent on a man: if he believes, you believe, and if he disbelieves, you disbelieve. If you must follow, then follow the dead, for the living is not safe from trial."

"Do not be an imma'a (a person without a mind of his own, a mere follower)."

They said: "What is the imma'a?"

He said: "He says, 'I am with the people: if they are guided, I am guided, and if they go astray, I go astray.' Rather, let each of you resolve that if the people disbelieve, he will not disbelieve."

A man said to him: "Teach me comprehensive and beneficial words."

He said: "Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him. Stay with the Qur'an wherever it goes. Whoever brings you the truth, accept it from him even if he is distant and hateful, and whoever brings you falsehood, reject it even if he is beloved and close."

A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: "Render your trust." He will say: "O Lord, from where, when the world has gone?" Then it will take the form of its appearance on the day he took it, in the depth of Hell. He will slip and take it, place it upon his shoulder, and climb with it until, when he thinks he is out with it, it will fall, and he will fall after it forever and ever.

"Seek your heart in three places: at the hearing of the Qur'an, in gatherings of remembrance, and in times of solitude. If you do not find it in these places, ask Allah to bestow a heart upon you, for you have no heart."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 74, verses 43–44:

And His saying, concerning the people of the Fire: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor.﴾

Since the purpose is to report about the one deserving to be fed, that they were stingy toward him, withheld from him his right to be fed, and their hearts were hardened toward him, mentioning him is the purpose, not the food.

Reflect on this method in the Qur'an: its mention of what is most important and its omission of what is less important reveals to you a gate of its inimitability (i'jaz) and the perfection of its eloquence.

(Section: the ruling on one who abandons fasting, Hajj and zakat)

Does one who abandons fasting, Hajj and zakat become like one who abandons prayer in terms of the obligation to kill him?

On this there are three narrations from Imam Ahmad.

The first: he is killed for abandoning all of them, just as he is killed for abandoning prayer.

The argument for this narration is that zakat, fasting and Hajj are pillars of Islam, so one is killed for abandoning them all, like prayer. For this reason, al-Siddiq fought those who withheld zakat and said:

"By God, I will fight whoever distinguishes between prayer and zakat, for they are companions in the Book of God."

Also, these pillars are among the rights of Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ did not order the cessation of fighting except for one who committed to the testimony of faith and its rights.

He also informed that the sanctity of blood is not established except by the right of Islam. So this is fighting against a group that refuses, and the killing of the individual who is subdued is only for his abandoning the rights of the testimony and the laws of Islam. This is the most sound of the opinions.

The second narration: one is not killed for abandoning anything other than prayer, because prayer is a purely physical act of worship into which substitution (niyabah) never enters, whereas Hajj, fasting and zakat admit of substitution.

Also, the saying of Abdullah ibn Shaqiq:

"The companions of Muhammad ﷺ did not consider abandoning any of the deeds to be disbelief except prayer."

And because prayer is distinguished from all other deeds by properties not found in others. It is the first thing God made obligatory of Islam, and for this reason the Prophet ﷺ instructed his deputies and messengers to begin calling people to it after the two testimonies.

He said to Mu'adh: "You will come to a people who are People of the Book, so let the first thing you call them to be the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that God has enjoined upon them five prayers in the day and night."

Also, it is the first deed for which a servant is called to account, and because God enjoined it in the heavens on the night of the Ascension (mi'raj), and because it is the most frequently mentioned obligation in the Qur'an, and because when the people of the Fire are asked ﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾ they did not begin with abandoning prayer.

Also, its obligation never drops from the servant in any circumstance as long as his intellect remains, unlike other obligations, which are required in some circumstances and not others.

Also, it is the pole of the tent of Islam, and when the pole falls, the tent falls.

Also, it is the last thing to be lost from the religion.

Also, it is obligatory upon the free and the slave, the male and the female, the resident and the traveler, the healthy and the sick, the rich and the poor.

The Messenger of God ﷺ would not accept from one who answered his call to Islam except with a commitment to prayer, as Qatadah said, narrating: "The Messenger of God ﷺ would not accept from one who answered his call to Islam except with the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat."

Also, the acceptance of all other deeds depends upon its performance, so God does not accept from one who abandons it fasting, Hajj, charity, jihad, or any of the deeds, as 'Awn ibn Abdullah said:

"When the servant enters his grave, he is questioned about his prayer first. If it is sound for him, he is then considered regarding the rest of his deeds. And if it is not sound for him, nothing of his deeds is considered after that."

This is indicated by the hadith in the Musnad and the Sunan narrated from Abu Hurairah from the Prophet ﷺ:

"The first thing for which a servant will be called to account of his deeds is his prayer. If it is sound, he has succeeded and prospered; and if it is corrupt, he has failed and lost."

And if any of the deeds of righteousness were accepted from him, he would not be among the failed and the losers.

The third narration: one is killed for abandoning zakat and fasting, but not for abandoning Hajj, because it is disputed whether it is to be performed immediately or may be delayed.

Whoever says it may be delayed says: how can one be killed for an obligation whose timing is broad?

This basis is very weak, for one who kills him for abandoning it does not kill him merely for delaying it. Rather, the true form of the question is that he resolves to abandon Hajj and says, "It is obligatory upon me, but I will never perform it."

This is the point of dispute. The correct view is that he is to be killed, because Hajj is among the rights of Islam, and sanctity is established for one who speaks the testimony of Islam except by its rights, and Hajj is the greatest of its rights.

The third and fourth attribute: plunging into falsehood (al-khawd bil-batil) and denying the truth. Thus there gathered for them the absence of sincerity (ikhlas) and beneficence (ihsan), plunging into falsehood, and denying the truth. And there gathered for the People of the Right (ashab al-yamin) sincerity, beneficence, affirming the truth, and speaking it. So their sincerity, their beneficence, their certainty and their speech were made upright. The People of the Left (ashab al-shimal), however, exchanged sincerity for shirk, beneficence for evil-doing, certainty for doubt and denial, and beneficial speech for plunging into falsehood. Therefore the intercession of the intercessors did not benefit them. That is, they had no intercessor on their behalf, because intercession would be made for them but would not benefit them. This is because they turned away from the Reminder, did not raise their heads to it at all, and recoiled from hearing it, as wild asses recoil from the lion or from the archers.

Then He concluded the surah by saying that He combined in it His legislation (shar') and His decree (qadar), and the establishment of proof against them by affirming their will and explaining what the requirement of tawhid and lordship is, and that this belongs to Him and not to them. The first is His justice ('adl), and the second is His grace (fadl). The first necessitates striving, seeking, and eagerness for what saves them, as they do in the affairs of their worldly interests, and even more so. The second necessitates seeking help, reliance (tawakkul), entrusting (tafwid), and turning in desire to the One in whose hand this is, so that it may be made easy for them and He may grant them success. And Allah is the One whose help is sought, and upon Him is reliance.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 74, verses 49–51:

He likened their aversion and flight from the Qur'an to donkeys (ḥumur) that see a lion (asad) or archers (rumāh) and flee from them. This is a marvelous analogy and illustration, for the people, in their ignorance of what Allah sent His Messenger with, are like donkeys, which understand nothing. When they hear the voice of the lion or the shooting, they flee from it with the utmost flight.

This is the ultimate blame for them, for they fled from the guidance in which lies their happiness and their life, like the flight of donkeys from what destroys and kills them. Within the word ﴿مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ (mustanfirah) there is a meaning more emphatic than ﴿نَافِرَةٌ﴾ (nāfirah), for because of the intensity of their flight, some of them have urged others to flee and exhorted them to it. In the form istif'āl (the tenth-type verbal pattern, here expressing request or seeking) there is an additional degree of meaning beyond the bare verb, so it is as though they had charged one another to flee and agreed upon it together. As for the one who reads it with a fatḥah on the fā' (mustafirah, as a passive/transitive form), the meaning is that the lion (qaswarah) roused them and drove them to flee by its might and its ferocity.
